main.title: God of War
main.subtitle: Kratos and Atreus beyond the Greek world
main.summary: God of War is a 2018 action-adventure game developed by Santa Monica Studio and published by Sony Interactive Entertainment.

cards.heading: A new beginning for God of War
cards.text: God of War is a 2018 action-adventure game developed by Santa Monica Studio and published by Sony Interactive Entertainment. It was released worldwide for the PlayStation 4 in April 2018, with a Windows port released in January 2022. It is the eighth game in the God of War series and the sequel to 2010's God of War III.

cards.heading: A father and son in Midgard
cards.text: While previous games were based on Greek mythology, God of War transitioned to Norse mythology, and takes place in mythical ancient Scandinavia in the realm of Midgard. Players control Kratos, who embarks on a journey with his son, Atreus, to scatter the ashes of Atreus's mother from the highest peak of the nine realms. Kratos keeps his past a secret from Atreus, who is unaware he is a demigod. Along their journey, they come into conflict with monsters and gods of the Norse world.

cards.heading: An axe and a closer viewpoint
cards.text: Described by creative director Cory Barlog as a reimagining of the franchise, a major gameplay change is that Kratos now uses a magical battle axe, the Leviathan Axe, instead of his signature double-chained blades. The game also uses an over-the-shoulder free camera, with the game in one shot, as opposed to the fixed cinematic camera of the previous entries. It also includes role-playing game elements, and Kratos's son Atreus provides assistance in combat. The majority of the original game's development team worked on God of War and designed it to be accessible and grounded. A short text-based game, A Call from the Wilds, was released in February 2018 through Facebook Messenger and follows Atreus on his first adventure. A smartphone app, Mímir's Vision, was released three days before the release, providing additional information about the Norse setting.

cards.heading: Reception, legacy and further stories
cards.text: God of War received acclaim for its story, world design, art direction, music, graphics, combat system, and characters, in particular the dynamic between Kratos and Atreus. Many reviewers felt it had successfully revitalized the series without losing its core identity. It was named Game of the Year by numerous media outlets and award shows, and has been cited as among the greatest video games. It sold more than five million copies within a month of release and had sold 23 million by November 2022, making it one of the best-selling PlayStation 4 games and the best-selling game in the series. A novelization was released in August 2018, followed by a prequel comic series published from November 2018 to June 2021, while a live-action television series is in development for Amazon Prime Video. A sequel, God of War Ragnarök, was released for the PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 in 2022, and for Windows in 2024.

main.title: Detroit: Become Human
main.subtitle: Three lives in one city
main.summary: Detroit: Become Human is Quantic Dream's interactive drama for PlayStation 4, released on 25 May 2018. Its near-future Detroit is home to androids built to serve people, and the story follows three whose situations begin to change. Kara tries to protect a young girl, Connor investigates androids who have departed from their programming, and Markus becomes involved in a movement for freedom. Switching between them lets the player see the same society from different positions. Decisions made during their chapters determine which paths through the larger crisis remain possible.

cards.heading: Three lives in one city
cards.text: Detroit: Become Human is Quantic Dream's interactive drama for PlayStation 4, released on 25 May 2018. Its near-future Detroit is home to androids built to serve people, and the story follows three whose situations begin to change. Kara tries to protect a young girl, Connor investigates androids who have departed from their programming, and Markus becomes involved in a movement for freedom. Switching between them lets the player see the same society from different positions. Decisions made during their chapters determine which paths through the larger crisis remain possible.

cards.heading: A conversation can close a route
cards.text: The player explores scenes, examines objects and chooses responses, often under pressure. What has been noticed can affect the options available when a conversation or confrontation reaches its decisive moment. Action sequences add timed inputs, and failure can send the story down another branch instead of simply demanding a restart. A character's survival is not guaranteed. The consequence makes attention to the immediate scene important even when its larger significance is unclear: a small observation may later supply the option that allows someone to escape a dangerous situation.

cards.heading: See the shape of the story
cards.text: A flowchart shown after each chapter records the route taken and indicates other branches without revealing every event. It gives the player's decisions a visible structure and makes another attempt a deliberate investigation of alternatives. David Cage and Adam Williams wrote the story, drawing on the earlier Kara technology demonstration. Each protagonist has a different composer: Philip Sheppard for Kara, Nima Fakhrara for Connor and John Paesano for Markus. The Windows release followed in 2019, bringing the same branching adventure to another platform after its PlayStation 4 debut.

main.title: Among Us
main.subtitle: Trust is part of the game
main.summary: Among Us is a 2018 online multiplayer social deduction game developed and published by the American game studio Innersloth.

cards.heading: A social-deduction game across platforms
cards.text: Among Us is a 2018 online multiplayer social deduction game developed and published by the American game studio Innersloth. The game allows for cross-platform play; it was released on iOS and Android devices in June 2018 and on Windows later that year in November. It was ported to the Nintendo Switch in December 2020 and on the PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S in December 2021.

cards.heading: Crewmates, Impostors and the meeting room
cards.text: Among Us takes place in space-themed settings where players are colorful, armless cartoon astronauts. Each player takes on one of two roles: most are Crewmates, but a small number are Impostors. Crewmates work to complete assigned tasks in the game while identifying and voting out suspected Impostors (who appear identical to Crewmates) using social deduction, while Impostors have the objective of killing the Crewmates. The game was inspired by the party game Mafia and the science fiction horror film The Thing.

cards.heading: A second life through streaming
cards.text: While the game was initially released in 2018 to little mainstream attention, it received a massive rise in popularity in 2020 due to many Twitch streamers and YouTubers playing it during the COVID-19 pandemic. It received favorable reviews from critics for fun and entertaining gameplay, and it has been considered among the greatest mobile video games of all time. The game and its stylized characters have been the subject of various internet memes.

cards.heading: An expanding franchise
cards.text: Following the game's success in 2020, it has received multiple updates and expanded into a multimedia franchise. An animated television adaptation has been announced, and Innersloth revealed the spinoff Among Us Story: On Guard in June 2026, while it was still in development.

main.title: Mario Tennis Aces
main.subtitle: A rally with another resource to manage
main.summary: Mario Tennis Aces is Camelot's Switch tennis game, released on 22 June 2018.

cards.heading: A rally with another resource to manage
cards.text: Mario Tennis Aces is Camelot's Switch tennis game, released on 22 June 2018. Mario and a broad cast compete through familiar strokes and more elaborate special techniques, turning a rally into a contest over positioning, timing and energy. Topspin, slices and lobs still define how the ball crosses the court, but a powerful opportunity can threaten the opponent's racket as well as the point. The player has to read both the direction of the next shot and the resources available for responding to it.

cards.heading: Protect the racket as well as the court
cards.text: Zone Shots allow precise targeting and can damage a defending racket unless the return is timed correctly. Repeated damage breaks it, with losing the last available racket ending the match. Zone Speed slows the surrounding action to help reach a distant ball, but spends the same energy used by other advanced techniques. Rallies and Trick Shots replenish that supply. A strong response therefore carries a cost, giving the player reasons to save energy, attempt a difficult block or use a safer stroke that keeps the exchange alive.

cards.heading: A sporting cast built around different strengths
cards.text: The character roster offers different combinations of reach, speed and power, with further competitors added through post-release tournaments and updates. An adventure mode places the mechanics within a sequence of special challenges, while multiplayer provides the continuing test of reading another person's choices. Motoi Sakuraba composed the music. Aces develops Mario Tennis around a useful tension: the expressive special moves create spectacular moments, but the next ordinary return can still determine whether the energy needed for another advantage will be available.

main.title: Octopath Traveler
main.subtitle: Eight starting points in Orsterra
main.summary: Octopath Traveler is Square Enix and Acquire's role-playing game, first released for Switch on 13 July 2018.

cards.heading: Eight starting points in Orsterra
cards.text: Octopath Traveler is Square Enix and Acquire's role-playing game, first released for Switch on 13 July 2018. Eight travelers begin in different parts of Orsterra, each with a personal story and a reason to leave home. The player chooses a starting protagonist and recruits the others while exploring the continent. Towns and routes connect those separate lives, letting the party grow around a first chosen viewpoint. Its HD-2D presentation gives the journeys a distinctive appearance through small character sprites placed within richly lit three-dimensional scenery.

cards.heading: Break a defense before spending the reserve
cards.text: Battles turn on breaking enemy defenses by striking weaknesses. The party can also save Boost Points and spend them to strengthen an action, connecting one turn's restraint to another turn's burst of power. Recognizing when an opponent is vulnerable matters as much as discovering the right weapon or element. The eight travelers bring different abilities to that preparation, while their actions outside combat provide ways to interact with townspeople. A useful encounter can therefore begin before a battle, through what a particular character can learn or obtain in town.

cards.heading: Sprites within a world of light
cards.text: Each traveler's story unfolds across four chapters, with the initial protagonist remaining in the active party until that arc is complete. The structure lets the player follow several ambitions across the same world while developing a preferred group for combat. Yasunori Nishiki composed the score, supporting the regions and individual character themes. The success of the visual approach helped make HD-2D a recognizable style for later projects. Octopath's identity rests on that combination of illustrated intimacy, luminous scenery and a party assembled from eight different departures.

main.title: WarioWare Gold
main.subtitle: Intelligent Systems · Nintendo 3DS
main.summary: WarioWare Gold is Intelligent Systems' Nintendo 3DS collection of over three hundred microgames. Wario stages a tournament with a large cash prize, expecting the proceedings to make him richer. The familiar cast supplies short stories and rapidly changing challenges, drawn from earlier games and new material. Each task arrives with only a moment to understand what is required. The collection makes that uncertainty its main pleasure: the player recognises a strange little situation, finds the necessary action and is immediately asked to understand another.

cards.heading: A tournament measured in seconds
cards.text: WarioWare Gold is Intelligent Systems' Nintendo 3DS collection of over three hundred microgames. Wario stages a tournament with a large cash prize, expecting the proceedings to make him richer. The familiar cast supplies short stories and rapidly changing challenges, drawn from earlier games and new material. Each task arrives with only a moment to understand what is required. The collection makes that uncertainty its main pleasure: the player recognises a strange little situation, finds the necessary action and is immediately asked to understand another.

cards.heading: The next action uses another part of the machine
cards.text: Some microgames require buttons, others use the touchscreen, microphone or the system's motion sensing. Their controls connect the collection to the different ways the series previously asked people to play. A brief prompt must become a useful movement before the time expires. Later rounds accelerate, reducing the pause between recognition and response. Lives allow a few mistakes, while boss challenges extend one idea into a longer task. The variety comes from changing the meaning of a small gesture, rather than teaching a complicated control scheme.

cards.heading: A collection with its own voices
cards.text: Gold gives the story sequences full voice acting and allows players to record alternative dialogue over them. Unlockable challenges alter the conditions around familiar microgames, introducing distractions or other constraints. Coins earned through play open further amusements and collectibles, supplying reasons to revisit the short routines. The game arrived late in the 3DS's life and gathered several generations of WarioWare around the capabilities of one machine. Its shifting inputs make the collection feel like a celebration of the hardware as well as the characters using it.

main.title: Dead Cells
main.summary: Dead Cells is a 2018 roguelike-Metroidvania game developed by Motion Twin.

cards.heading: Death, collected Cells and lasting upgrades
cards.text: Dead Cells is a 2018 roguelike-Metroidvania game developed by Motion Twin. The player takes the role of an amorphous creature called the Prisoner. As the Prisoner, the player must fight their way out of a diseased island in order to slay the island's King. The player gains weapons, treasure and other tools through exploration of the procedurally generated levels. Dead Cells features a permadeath system, causing the player to lose all items and other abilities upon dying. A currency called Cells can be collected from defeated enemies, allowing the player to purchase permanent upgrades.

cards.heading: A browser-game follow-up changes direction
cards.text: Production of Dead Cells began after Motion Twin planned development for a follow-up to their previous browser game Die2Nite. The developers decided to replace the cooperative gameplay of Die2Nite with a single-player experience focused around combat and action. They took inspiration from the Engineer character class from Team Fortress 2, and remade Dead Cells into an action platform game where the player would utilize a variety of combinations of weapons and skills.

cards.heading: Ports, continuing support and reception
cards.text: The game was released for Linux, macOS, Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, Windows, and Xbox One on August 7, 2018. A mobile port for iOS was released on August 28, 2019, and an Android port was released in 2020. A version for PlayStation 5 was added on June 29, 2023. After release, the game was supported with several updates and expansions, with developmental duties handled by Evil Empire. The game received positive reviews from critics, who praised its combat, visuals, and permadeath system. By June 2023, the game had sold over 10 million copies.

main.title: Xbox Adaptive Controller
main.subtitle: Controls arranged around the player
main.summary: Two large buttons form a hub for switches, joysticks and other assistive devices. The Xbox Adaptive Controller makes the arrangement of physical controls a design choice shaped around each player.

cards.heading: Controls arranged around the player
cards.text: The Xbox Adaptive Controller turns a controller into a configurable system. Two large programmable buttons sit on a central hub, while external switches, buttons and joysticks can be connected and arranged around a player. Microsoft developed the device with players with limited mobility and accessibility organizations, treating physical differences as design requirements. It reached commercial release on 4 September 2018.

cards.heading: Connecting a personal set of inputs
cards.text: External switches, joysticks and buttons connect to the hub?s ports. A control can be placed wherever the player can most comfortably reach it, rather than remaining in a fixed gamepad grip. Different inputs can be distributed across a desk, board or wheelchair mounting.

cards.heading: Developed with players and accessibility organisations
cards.text: Microsoft worked with players with limited mobility and organisations including AbleGamers, the Cerebral Palsy Foundation, SpecialEffect and Warfighter Engaged. Their feedback guided the inputs, connections and physical arrangement of the controller.

cards.heading: An easier box to open
cards.text: The packaging was also developed with testers. Tabs, loops and an opening structure reduced the strength and fine hand movements needed to reach the device. Unboxing became part of the accessibility work alongside setting up and using the controls.

features.title: Fit the player
features.summary: The arrangement belongs to its user.

cards.heading: A photograph starts a conversation
cards.text: Microsoft's account traces the Xbox Adaptive Controller to an engineer seeing a custom device made by Warfighter Engaged in 2014. Conversations with its founder, Ken Jones, led into employee hackathon experiments. Another change came with Copilot, which allowed two controllers to work together. The adaptive device could become a separate unit rather than an attachment squeezed onto a standard pad. Its eventual form grew from existing players' arrangements and several rounds of work, joining a wider system of controls instead of demanding one grip.

cards.heading: Read a port without turning it over
cards.text: The controller's details addressed practical acts around a gaming session. Nineteen sockets ran along its rear edge, with identifying marks embossed above them and grooves helping a user guide plugs into place. Threaded inserts offered ways to attach the device to a wheelchair, board or desk. Microsoft described these choices as responses to players' feedback. Setting up could be part of the design problem alongside pressing a button: a usable arrangement needed connections somebody could identify and a device that would stay where they needed it.

cards.heading: The same diagnosis, different needs
cards.text: In a 2023 interview, Sony's Alvin Daniel remembered an early test that changed the Access controller team's approach. Two participants with cerebral palsy needed very different accommodations: one benefited from support for a conventional controller, while another could not operate it with their hands. Medical categories had not supplied a single useful layout. Working with players and expert organisations, the team turned towards the barriers presented by the controller itself. The question became how a particular person could reach and operate it, allowing arrangements to differ and change over time.

cards.heading: Let the sticks find their place
cards.text: Access placed larger buttons in one plane and supplied interchangeable caps with different shapes and textures. Daniel also described using two Access controllers, or pairing one with a DualSense, so the sticks could sit at different distances, heights and orientations. AbleGamers, Stack Up and SpecialEffect helped the team consider existing mounts and switches around the player. The controller arrived as part of that adaptable environment. Its useful shape could continue to emerge after purchase, as someone arranged the pieces to suit the way they played.
